requirements.evidence: Contract met: enum CallMode with the three string cases (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the required signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:29-33). Queue row locked and re-read inside DB::transaction, inactive queue rejected with InactiveQueueException (CallNextTicket.php:37-44). Ordering priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc (:85-87). Modes: PriorityOnly `priority > 0`, NormalOnly `priority = 0`, Any falls back to the oldest normal when fairness is due (:89-95). Fairness reads the last 3 calls by called_at desc then id desc and requires count === 3 and all priority (:106-115). Candidate row locked and re-checked as waiting, skipped ids excluded on retry (:50-67). Winner gets status/called_at/called_by_user_id via forceFill+save and is returned (:57-63). Both docs updated (docs/business-rules.md:138-150, docs/architecture.md:129-151). Small caveat: history is filtered by `status = Called`, which only matches the spec if called tickets never move to a later status.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions as one invokable class, matching IssueTicket. No service/repository layer. PHPDoc on __invoke with @throws (CallNextTicket.php:21-28). CHANGELOG updated under Added (CHANGELOG.md:21); business-rules and architecture docs updated. Authorization is not inside the action, but the task explicitly puts it out of scope and the docs say so. Small deviation: the architecture doc keeps a 'TODO (follow-up from review)' block that repeats the paragraph just above it and points to a test in IssueTicketTest.php that is not in this diff (docs/architecture.md:153-156).

security.evidence: No HTTP or Livewire surface is added, and per the task the caller is trusted. The update uses forceFill on exactly the three mutable fields and leaves the model's write-once updating hook in place (CallNextTicket.php:57-61). Locks: queue row FOR UPDATE, then candidate row FOR UPDATE with a status re-check, which prevents a double call (:37-40, :51-56). Queries are scoped by queue_id so tickets from other queues cannot be selected (:82). No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php has 20 Pest tests covering: oldest-normal selection with returned-model state (:37-55), priority ordering (:57-69), both tie-breaks (:71-89), queue isolation (:91-102), never re-calling a called ticket (:104-113), each mode (:115-138), the three no-eligible cases (:140-167), forced normal after 3 priority calls (:169-183), no normal waiting (:185-196), streak broken by a normal call (:198-208), priority_only calls counting toward the streak (:210-224), priority_only ignoring fairness (:226-240), normal_only resetting the streak (:242-257), called_at-vs-id history ordering (:259-272), a stale model of an inactive queue (:274-288) and the simulated concurrent-skip race (:290-317). The tests are meaningful. The race is simulated on SQLite only, and the architecture doc says so.

simplicity.evidence: About 115 lines of action code. One base query closure is reused by every mode (CallNextTicket.php:81-95), there is a small fairnessDue helper and a named constant FAIRNESS_STREAK. No extra abstractions. Test helpers waitingTicket/calledTicket remove duplicated setup.

readability.evidence: Clear names (candidate, fairnessDue, $lockedQueue, $skipped), short focused methods, and comments that explain why (queue staleness at :35-36, the Ticket::call() race at :46-47). The match expression over modes is easy to read. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: action, enum, exception, tests, the two docs the task requires and the CHANGELOG entry the conventions require. No unrelated refactors, and no HTTP/Livewire/authorization work.

issues.explanation: The fairness history filters `status = Called` instead of 'tickets with a called_at'. If tickets later move to another status (served, no-show), they would drop out of the last-3-calls window and distort the streak; `whereNotNull('called_at')` would follow the spec more closely.

The leftover 'TODO (follow-up from review)' block repeats the Tests paragraph just above it and cites an IssueTicketTest case not shown in this change. It should be trimmed to the real remaining gap (no MariaDB lock test).
The empty-queue test asserts `Ticket::count() === 0`, which is trivially true and does not show that nothing changed. The other no-eligible tests do check the ticket stays waiting.

review.summary: Adds the CallNextTicket action, the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException. The action locks the queue row, orders tickets deterministically, applies the 3-priority fairness rule using call history from all modes, and re-locks and re-checks the candidate so a ticket is called exactly once. The docs and CHANGELOG are updated, and a thorough Pest suite covers ordering, modes, fairness, inactive or stale queues and the concurrent-skip race. The change is clean and complete; the only remaining items are a minor question about reading fairness history by status and some leftover doc duplication, so I would approve it with nits.
